mappings.note: Queen Didda consolidating power in Kashmir, eliminating rivals, founding towns and restoring temples. LO-32 for the exercise of royal authority; LO-43 is added as the frame's only women-focused outcome, though it is framed around disadvantage rather than a reigning queen.
Chola inscriptions praising the ruler in Sanskrit while recording grant terms in the local language. LO-32 for the grant as administration, CG-SST2 for reading the inscription as a source.
Chola prosperity built on efficient administration, a powerful navy and Kaveri delta irrigation. Administrative measures and military capacity together, LO-32.
The Aulikaras of Dashapura breaking Huna power by repeated defeats. Military strategy of a kingdom, LO-32.

Why 600-1200 CE matters - regional kingdoms, cultural growth, trade, resilience against invasion. A question about the character of a period; goal-level CG-SST2, matching the other periodisation item.

Sorts true Chola claims - empire, navy, bilingual patronage - from the false claim that they wrecked Kaveri agriculture. Kingdom's capacity and policy, LO-32. (Stem survives only as its last line; see report.)
Narasimhavarman I, 'Mamalla', capturing Badami after defeating Pulakeshin II. Military strategy, LO-32.

Chera copper plates recording Christian, Muslim and Jewish traders in Kerala. An inscription used as evidence of the period's trade and plurality; goal-level CG-SST2 rather than LO-32, since no measure of rule is at issue.
Assertion-reason on Arab rulers in Sindh permitting temple rebuilding because resistance made replacement impossible. Governing strategy under constraint, LO-32.
The monolithic Bahubali at Shravanabelagola. Monumental religious sculpture and its carving; LO-34 is the nearest outcome, being the frame's only one on the making of religious monuments.

Bhaskara I on trigonometry and Virahanka on the early Fibonacci sequence, against the false claim that Arab scholars ignored Indian astronomy. History of science and its transmission, goal-level CG-SST2. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)
The multiplication of jatis as a sign of a complex, occupationally differentiated society. Social history of the period, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Rajatarangini's significance - built from inscriptions, grants and earlier chronicles, and judging rulers morally. Source criticism, the clearest goal-level CG-SST2 fit in the chapter.
Vikramashila's six colleges, its international students, and its scholars shaping Vajrayana in Tibet. CG-SST2 for the institution of learning, LO-35 for the religious school it carried outward.

Rashtrakuta conquest set against their patronage, above all the rock-cut Kailashanatha. LO-32 for the military expansion, LO-34 for the temple - the question explicitly asks for the balance between the two.
Vatapi as a fortified base that halted Harsha's advance and as a centre of rock-cut Hindu and Jain temples. LO-32 for the military role, LO-34 for the cave temples.

Women in governance: patriarchal succession set against Tribhuvana Mahadevi I suppressing rebellion and issuing her own grants. LO-43 for the position of women, LO-32 for the administrative authority actually exercised.
Brahmagupta's work translated in Baghdad, and the decimal system and zero reaching Europe. Transmission of knowledge, goal-level CG-SST2.
Match-list pairing the Tripartite Struggle and land grants (LO-32) with bhakti devotion (LO-35) and merchant guilds. LO-32 and LO-35 cover the two scored strands. (Fragmentary stem; see report.)
Harshavardhana as the Pushyabhuti ruler acceding in 606 CE. Dynastic recall, LO-32.
Kannauj as Harsha's capital. Seat of a kingdom, LO-32.
Xuanzang as the pilgrim of Harsha's reign. A foreign traveller's account as a source, goal-level CG-SST2, matching the other Xuanzang items.
Names the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas as the three contenders. Strategy for control of Kannauj, LO-32.
Gopala as founder of the Pala line in 750 CE. Dynastic recall, LO-32.
Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkotas defeating an Arab chief three times. Military record, LO-32; the Rajatarangini is only the vehicle here, so CG-SST2 is not added.

'Monsoon' from the Arabic mawsim, a word carried by seasonal Arabian Sea trade. Linguistic evidence of historical contact, goal-level CG-SST2; LO-28 is rejected because the question is etymological, not climatic.
Karaikal Ammaiyar as the 6th-century woman saint-poet among the Nayanars. LO-36, the bhakti-poetry outcome; LO-35 is reserved for items explaining why the movement arose.

The Chola Nataraja bronze as Shiva's cosmic dance of creation and destruction. Religious art and its iconography; LO-34 is the nearest outcome this frame offers, being its only one on the making of religious images and monuments.
The Tripartite Struggle's significance, ending with no lasting victor and all three exhausted. LO-32 for the contest for control, LO-33 because the answer weighs the three powers against each other.
Pallava contribution: monolithic rock-cut temples at Mamallapuram (LO-34) alongside Kanchi's spice and silk trade and overseas connections (CG-SST2, no LO covering the period's commerce).
The Bhakti tradition's evolution under the Alvars and Nayanars. LO-35 for the movement's emergence and inclusiveness, LO-36 for the devotional poetry it produced - the question asks for both.
Land grants creating a landholding class, extending cultivation, and shifting power away from the centre. An administrative measure and its consequences, LO-32.

Merchant guilds uniting artisans, traders and moneylenders, running markets and financing maritime commerce. Economic history of the period, goal-level CG-SST2; C-SST4.2 is rejected as it concerns visiting a present-day local market.
Harsha's governance, campaigns, tolerance and patronage as the ideal of kingship. Administrative and military measures of a ruler, LO-32.
Hunas moving from invaders to administrators and soldiers within Indian polities. Absorption into the machinery of kingdoms, LO-32.

The Arab invasions' long-term political effect, contained to Sindh by resistance from rulers such as Nagabhata I. Military strategy and its outcome, LO-32. (Answer breaks off at a watermark; see report.)
Vikramashila as Dharmapala's foundation. Royal patronage, LO-32, consistent with the earlier Dharmapala item.
King Bhoja's title Adi Varaha. Royal titulature, LO-32.
Dantidurga founding the independent Rashtrakuta line. Dynastic founding, LO-32.
Krishna I as patron of the Ellora Kailashanatha. The temple itself is what is being recalled, so LO-34 rather than LO-32.
Kalhana as author of the Rajatarangini. Identification of a source, goal-level CG-SST2.
Pulakeshin II as the Chalukya who checked Harsha. Military outcome between two kingdoms, LO-32.
Kanchi as the Pallava capital. Seat of a kingdom, LO-32.
Narasimhavarman I as 'Mamalla'. Royal title, LO-32.
Madurai as the Pandya capital. Seat of a kingdom, LO-32.
Vijayalaya as founder of the revived Cholas. Dynastic recall, LO-32.
Samantas as the subordinate rulers who ran local administration. The vocabulary of the period's administrative structure - a direct LO-32 fit.
Kayasthas as the scribal jati of the period. Social history, goal-level CG-SST2, matching the other jati items.
Tribhuvana Mahadevi I of the Bhauma-Karas. LO-32 for a sovereign's identity, LO-43 as the frame's only outcome touching women's position.
Bahubali as the monolithic Jain statue at Shravanabelagola. Monumental religious sculpture, LO-34.
Brahmagupta on zero and negative numbers. History of science, goal-level CG-SST2.
The Hunas as the Central Asian invaders of the 6th century. Military history of the period, LO-32.
Muhammad bin Qasim as commander of the Sindh conquest. Military strategy, LO-32.
Hindu-Arabic numerals as the system the Arabs carried to Europe. Transmission of knowledge, goal-level CG-SST2.
Banabhatta as author of the Harshacharita. Identification of a source, goal-level CG-SST2. (The stored answer runs on into an unrelated case study; see report.)

This row's stem is two questions run together; the scored content is the case study its answer resolves - Kanchipuram guilds of ship-owners, artisans and moneylenders funding a temple, and what maritime trade did for the economy. CG-SST2 for the commerce and guild patronage, LO-32 for part (a), which asks which dynasty ruled. (Merged stem; see report.)
Case study on three empires grinding each other down over Kannauj. LO-32 for the contest for control and why the city was worth it, LO-33 for part (c), which weighs the consequences across all three.
